answer: Make every new identity pass a proof-of-continuity pulse: it must reproduce a random slice of its own prior attestation history signed by the same key, and the required history length scales quadratically with the number of keys funded by one parent wallet. A copper-plated botnet can brute-force cheap keys, but each k-th clone needs twice the signed history of the last, so its cost curve bends past any honest budget. Wire kin keys to one jointly-slashed basalt bond: when any clone equivocates, the entire sibling set is slashed together.
